intent: Return the geometry to iteration 5's configuration (wheel_track 0.10 m, five sensors at y=0.08 spanning x=±0.06, 12 mm footprints), which is the best-scoring and only stable oval design so far. Iteration 8 showed that widening the row to ±0.07 cut the oval finish rate to 0.45 and the s-bend progress to 0.18. Keeping the geometry at the proven baseline lets the Integrator's controller work on a stable platform. Expected: oval finish at least 0.85, s-bend progress near 0.42, slalom line losses at about 1.0 with progress near 0.10, and a score near 386.
learning: Iteration 8 shows that the ±0.07 row hurts both the oval and the s-bend at 0.10 m, so the slalom line-loss gain from the wider row is not worth the cost. Iteration 7 showed the same pattern. The row width at ±0.06 is a stable setting, and the slalom needs a different lever. Ask the Integrator: with the ±0.06 row restored, does the slalom still lose the line once per run, and at which direction change? If the slalom line loss is at a sharp direction change, the next geometry test should be sensor spacing (for example, a denser centre cluster at the same ±0.06 span) rather than a wider reach. Also ask whether the oval finish rate returns to 1.0 with this geometry, which would confirm that the row width caused the iteration 7 and 8 collapses.
rationale: Iteration 8 tested the widened row (x=±0.07) at wheel_track 0.10 m, and it went backwards. Oval finish fell from 20 of 20 (iteration 5) to 9 of 20, and the s-bend progress fell from 0.42 to 0.18. The row change is the common factor, because iteration 5 had the same 0.10 m track with the ±0.06 row and was stable. Iteration 7 also fell when the row was widened, so the ±0.07 row is the likely cause of both oval collapses, not the track. The one benefit was slalom line losses falling from 1.0 to 0.0 per run, but the slalom still goes off track at progress 0.12, so the benefit is not enough to offset the oval and s-bend losses. The Integrator's decision rule for this case is to return the row to ±0.06 at y=0.08. Iteration 5 is the best-scoring design (386.35) and the only one with a stable oval, so I return to its exact geometry: five sensors at y=0.08 with x=-0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06, 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.10, wheels 0.03 m, mass 0.7 kg, body 0.12 by 0.18 m. The off-track floor binds at 0.06 m for every body width, so body changes stay out of scope. Expected result: oval finish at least 0.85 (near 1.0), s-bend progress near 0.42, and a score near iteration 5's. The slalom remains the open problem, and the only geometry lever I have left untested at the 0.10 track is sensor spacing or count, which I would test only after the stable baseline is confirmed.
